title: Micro-merge garden: surgical PR checklist & follow-ups
content:
Context and intent:
This is a personal scratchpad for a "micro-merge" workflow — small, surgical PRs that are deliberately gardened rather than rushed. Goal: reduce friction and rollbacks for high-churn areas (routing, batching, small kernel tweaks). Use as both a reviewer cheat-sheet and a post-merge todo list.

Quick philosophy:
- Prefer many tiny, well-tested changes over one large rollup.
- Every PR should be mergeable with a clear fallback path and a minimal blast radius.
- Keep reviewer burden <30 minutes unless the change truly needs architecture review.

Incoming PR triage (first pass, <5m):
- Is the PR <= 150 lines? If not, ask author to split.
- Does title + first comment explain: what, why, rollback plan? If not, request expansion.
- Labels: area:serving-runtime / area:routing / perf/regression-risk. Add if missing.
- CI green? If CI failure unrelated to change (flake), comment and re-run; if related, block.

Surgical review checklist (aim for 20–30m):
1) Correctness and intent:
   - Read the top-level description and diff. Can I explain the change in one sentence?
   - Edge cases: nil/empty inputs, negative path, timeouts — do tests cover them?
2) Tests:
   - Unit tests added for new logic? If none, request at least one focused test.
   - Is there an integration or e2e signal impacted (routing, kv-cache)? If yes, mark for soak.
3) Performance/perf-picture:
   - Is there a per-request or per-token hot path touched (kernel selection, batching)? If yes, ask for microbench or cite perf rationale.
   - Any allocations or copies introduced? Spot-check for additional buffer copies.
4) Observability and telemetry:
   - New metrics/error codes instrumented? If behavioral change, add a metric or a log line with sampling.
   - Are log messages structured and rate-limited?
5) Backwards compatibility:
   - Config defaults unchanged? If changed, ensure feature flag or rollouts configured.
6) Security and secrets:
   - Any env/config changes that touch keys/KMS? Route to security for sign-off.
7) Safety/QA gating:
   - Add a short checklist comment in PR linking to any manual QA steps (e.g., simulate burst, region fallback).

Merge gating heuristics (pre-merge checklist):
- If change touches serving runtime hotpath + >1 microservice: require 2 reviewers and an explicit canary plan.
- If change is small (<=3 files, <=150 lines) and low-risk labels: one reviewer + author can self-merge after 1 hour if no CI issues.
- Add a short rollback paragraph to PR body (commands, tag to revert to, smoke-checks).

Smoke and soak plan (post-merge):
- Smoke (first 30 minutes): verify latency P50/P95 for a small synthetic workload in prod-like staging.
- Soak (next 24h): route 5–10% traffic or orange canary; watch error rate, latency, token-cost; set alert thresholds 3x baseline for the first 3 hours.

Rollback steps (keep in PR body):
- Revert PR on GitHub (link): immediate if error rate spikes >X% or latency regression >Y%.
- If revert fails, fallback to previous model variant / lower-tier routing policy.
- Post-rollback: open a triage thread with timestamps, stack traces, correlation ids.

Post-merge follow-ups (add as GitHub todo checklist):
- Add a perf microbenchmark if one doesn't exist for the hot path.
- Add one more unit test for the edge case found during review.
- If a new metric was added, wire it into the per-route dashboard.
- Create a short runbook snippet for oncall describing how to identify and mitigate the specific regression.

Refactor idea seeds (quick notes for future PRs):
- Extract small kernel of decision logic in router -> make pure function, add property tests.
- Replace ad-hoc feature flags with a single feature-flag helper that logs rollout metadata.
- Centralize copy-on-write buffer helpers to avoid repeated defensive copies across handlers.

Low-effort automation ideas:
- Bot that enforces PR body template: requires rollback paragraph and labels before merging.
- Lint that flags diffs touching "hot" files without a perf bench file nearby.
- Small GitHub action: run a synthetic 1k-request latency check against staging for any PR labeled perf-risk.

Reviewer-facing phrases to use (short, actionable):
- "Split the non-essential refactor into a follow-up PR so this stays focused"
- "Can you add a targeted unit test for X edge-case?"
- "Please add a one-line rollback plan to the PR body"

Common pitfalls I keep seeing:
- Large PRs that mix behavioral change with cosmetic refactor.
- Missing telemetry for user-visible behavior changes.
- Skipping canaries because "small change" — small changes can interact in prod.

Open questions / notes to self:
- What threshold for latency regression should auto-revert? (capture baseline and discuss with SRE)
- Can we add a canned canary template for the console? (save time for reviewers)
- Follow up with Lina on adding a "hot file" tag list to repo metadata.

Short checklist to paste into PR body:
- [ ] Description: what + why + rollback
- [ ] CI: green (unit + smoke)
- [ ] Tests: added/updated for edge cases
- [ ] Observability: metric/log or justification
- [ ] Perf: bench or low-risk justification
- [ ] Rollout: canary plan or FF guard

End-of-doc: quick timestamped log for this scratchpad:
- 2024-11-07: initial draft after reviewing three small routing PRs during triage
- 2024-11-14: refined checklist, added automation ideas (TODO: open DX-automation ticket)

Notes-to-self: stash this in a reusable template (CONTRIBUTING or PR_TEMPLATE) once we iterate twice.
